questions.stem: A 16-year-old boy died due to an electric shock while playing near an electric post. His body was disfigured due to the high voltage. Permanent impairment of fingerprint pattern occurs in?
questions.solutionHtml:
All the above
  • Ridge alteration occurs in eczema, acanthosis nigricans, scleroderma, and dry or atrophic skin.
  • Permanent impairment of the fingerprint pattern occurs in leprosy. electric injury and after exposure to radiation.
  • In infantile paralysis, rickets ,and acromegaly, though the pattern is not altered, the distance between the ridges can be changed.



The Essentials of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd Edition, Page Number 87 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 63

questions.stem: A partial fingerprint was obtained from a crime scene at a hotel, the points of similarity for the identification of the killer should be at least?
questions.solutionHtml:
10
  • In practice, 10 to 12 points of fine comparison are accepted as proof of identity.
  • The patterns are not inherited and paternity cannot be proved through fingerprint patterns. The pattern is different even in identical twins.
  • The fingerprint patterns are distinctive and permanent in individuals.



The Essentials of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd Edition, Page Number 86 & 35th Edition, Page Number 62,63

questions.stem: From a crime scene, chance impressions were obtained with no definite patterns of fingerprints, next study for identifying the killer is by?
questions.solutionHtml:
Poroscopy
  • The ridges on fingers and hands are studded with microscopic pores, formed by mouths of ducts of subepidermal sweat glands.
  • Each millimetre of a ridge contains 9 to 18 pores. These pores are permanent and unchanged during their lifetime and vary in size, shape, width, starting, and stopping on occasion and branching at points, position, extent and number, distribution and arrangement of the pores over a given length of the ridge in each individual.
  • This method of examining pores is called poroscopy and is useful when only fragments of fingerprints are available in which there is no specific pattern.



The Essentials of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd Edition, Page Number 86 & 35th Edition, Page Number - 62,63

questions.stem: A film actress was found dead in the hotel room. The police suspect homicide on the primary analysis of the crime scene. While obtaining fingerprints from the suspects they found a suspect with burns all over the palm. Find the incorrect statement:

options.label: A
options.text: Criminals attempt to mutilate fingerprints by self-inflicted wounds or burns

options.label: B
options.text: In the case of pre-death struggle, the fingerprints of the assailant will remain on the victim even before death

options.label: C
options.text: Fingerprints can be obtained from decomposed bodies

options.label: D
options.text: Permanent impairment of the fingerprint pattern is seen in leprosy, electric injury, and after exposure to radiation.

questions.answerText: In the case of pre-death struggle, the fingerprints of the assailant will remain on the victim even before death
questions.solutionHtml:
In the case of pre-death struggle, the fingerprints of the assailant will remain on the victim even before death
  • The fingerprint of the assailant will remain on the victim only after death.
  • During the pre-death struggle, both the assailant and the victim will sweat due to nervous tension. After death, the victim will not sweat due to which fingerprints will be left on the body.



The Essentials of Forensic Medicine And Toxicology, 33rd Edition, Page Number 87 & 35th Edition, Page Number – 63

questions.stem: A fetus was brought for a postmortem examination. The center of ossification of which one of the following is used as medicolegal evidence for fetal viability:
questions.solutionHtml:
Distal end of femur

The centre of ossification for the lower end of the femur appears at 9 months, which is the age of maturity of the fetus and hence the best answer.




KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 34th Edition, Page Number: 72 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 53,54
